{"name":"release/10.0","commit":{"sha":"00a171f44e0777fd09369c5f0fcb5d1f2cfe07c1","node_id":"C_kwDODI9FZdoAKDAwYTE3MWY0NGUwNzc3ZmQwOTM2OWM1ZjBmY2I1ZDFmMmNmZTA3YzE","commit":{"author":{"name":"Johan Lorensson","email":"lateralusx.github@gmail.com","date":"2026-10-23T22:10:29Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-10-23T22:10:29Z"},"message":"[release/10.0] Filter leading GC polling frames from EventPipe stacks.- #136077 (#136091)

Fixes Issue dotnet/runtime#135050

main PR dotnet/runtime#135219

# Description

Manually adapted backport of dotnet/runtime#135219 to `release/10.0`,
corresponding to the .NET 11 backport in dotnet/runtime#136077.

EventPipe sampling suspension can cause threads to enter the managed GC
polling helpers, which then appear at the top of captured stacks and
obscure the actual workload.

Make `PollGCWorker` binder-visible and bind it during runtime startup,
allowing the EventPipe stack walker to omit leading `PollGC` and
`PollGCWorker` frames without loading methods during suspension.
Preserve caller frames, samples, and sample classification.

The backport uses `Thread.CoreCLR.cs` and the feature guards appropriate
to .NET 10, preserving its existing null-control-PC handling. Regression
coverage is added to the existing `GCEvents` test project because .NET
10 does not have the newer `SampleProfilerSampleType` test.

# Customer Impact

CPU-sampling profiles can attribute almost all samples to `PollGCWorker`
instead of the application workload, making performance investigations
misleading. This is a profiling artifact, not evidence of equivalent CPU
usage or GC pressure.

# Regression

Yes. The issue was reported as a regression from .NET 9 to .NET 10 after
GC polling moved into managed helpers. The regression was reproduced
locally on the unfixed .NET 10 runtime.

# Testing

Validated locally on Windows x64 with Checked CoreCLR and Release
libraries.

Build commands, all completed successfully with the local-only build
prerequisites described below:

```cmd
build.cmd clr+libs+host -rc Checked -lc Release -hc Release
src\tests\build.cmd -Test tracing\eventpipe\eventsvalidation\GCEvents.csproj x64 Checked -Priority 1 -SkipNative /p:LibrariesConfiguration=Release /p:HostConfiguration=Release
build.cmd clr -rc Checked -lc Release -hc Release
src\tests\build.cmd -GenerateLayoutOnly x64 Checked /p:LibrariesConfiguration=Release /p:HostConfiguration=Release
```

Test commands:

```cmd
set CORE_ROOT=C:\git\runtime\artifacts\tests\coreclr\windows.x64.Checked\Tests\Core_Root
pushd C:\git\runtime\artifacts\tests\coreclr\windows.x64.Checked\tracing\eventpipe\eventsvalidation\GCEvents
"%CORE_ROOT%\corerun.exe" GCEvents.dll
echo Exit code: %ERRORLEVEL%
popd
```

- Before the fix: the existing GC-events test passed, and the new
regression failed with exit code **101**, reporting a GC polling helper
at the top of a sample. Zero events were lost.
- After the fix: both tests passed with exit code **100**, checking
**9,430 sample stacks** with zero lost events.

Also ran `GCEvents.dll` with `DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0`: both tests
passed with exit code **100**, checking **9,943 sample stacks** with
zero lost events.

The regression checks raw sample stacks, retention of workload frames in
managed samples, and retention of workload frames in ordinary event
stacks.

Other platforms and configurations have not been validated for this
backport.

# Risk

Low. The change is narrowly scoped to identifying GC polling helpers and
omitting them only while they are leading frames in an EventPipe stack.
It does not change GC polling or suspension semantics, discard samples,
or change sample classification.

The worker is bound before managed execution, avoiding method loading
during stack walks. Existing handling of other frames is preserved.
Local testing confirmed the original failure and verified both the
regression and existing GC-events coverage after the fix, with default
tiering and tiering disabled.

Resolves dotnet/runtime#135050
